extracted.intended_audience: ICLR 2025 authors, reviewers, area chairs, and prospective reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Official FAQ summarizing ICLR 2025 policies and practical rules relevant to submitting papers, reporting concerns, reviewer duties, and conflict/dual-submission/contemporaneous-work rules. Useful for authors, reviewers, and area chairs interacting with OpenReview and the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting about ICLR reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: You must write a comment on OpenReview for the paper in question. You can restrict the visibility to only the area chairs, or reviewers, or the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not email the program chairs. Contacting PC directly for issues that can be best tackled by AC will only add delays. We receive a large volume of emails and the area chair is the right person to contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism should be reported by writing a comment on OpenReview for the paper in question. The public may now comment on any paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed, concrete evidence, and it will be factored into the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer registration status
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer sign-up for ICLR 2025 is closed; prospective reviewers cannot register now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you missed registration, you cannot sign up at this time (FAQ response: 'No, the reviewer registration is closed.').

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal reviewing requirement (review load)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected review load is 3 papers per reviewer as part of the reciprocal reviewing policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs/SACs/other service roles for ICLR 2025 are exempt from the requirement. If you cannot review according to the reciprocal reviewing policy you should request an exception via the provided form.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to sign up to fulfill reciprocal reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: To sign up as a reviewer to fulfill the reciprocal reviewing requirement, register using the link on iclr.cc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If exemption is needed, use the exception form referenced in the FAQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines are final — no extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract and main paper deadlines cannot be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extensions are possible. The dates are final. They will not be extended under any circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author list finalization after abstract deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The author list for each submission is finalized after the abstract deadline; no authors may be added or removed after that point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy is applied uniformly to all papers. There are no exceptions under any circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract submission procedure and review status
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit the abstract on OpenReview; uploading the PDF is not required until the full paper submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract will not be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When papers become public
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers will become public immediately once submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware that submissions are publicly visible on submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of contemporaneous/concurrent work
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are considered contemporaneous if they are published within the last four months relative to the full paper deadline (i.e., since July 1 for an Oct 1 deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That means, since our full paper deadline is October 1, if a paper was published (i.e., at a peer-reviewed venue) on or after July 1, 2024, authors are not required to compare their own work to that paper. Authors are encouraged to cite and discuss all relevant papers, but they may be excused for not knowing about papers not published in peer-reviewed conference proceedings or journals, which includes papers exclusively available on arXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions that are identical (or substantially similar) to versions that have been previously published, accepted for publication, or submitted in parallel to other conferences or journals are not allowed and violate the dual submission policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, papers that cite previous related work by the authors and papers that have appeared on non-peer reviewed websites (like arXiv) or that are currently under review or have been presented at workshops (venues without publication proceedings) do not violate the policy. The policy is enforced during the whole reviewing process period after the full paper submission deadline (Oct 1, 2024). Submission of the paper to archival repositories such as arXiv is allowed during the review period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise — domain relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience in vision or natural language processing (NLP) is considered relevant experience for reviewer roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such expertise can provide valuable insights into submissions that involve these topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal considerations in submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers addressing societal considerations are allowed in submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They will be evaluated according to the established reviewer guidelines (see Reviewer Guide).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request exceptions to reciprocal reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: If you cannot meet the reciprocal reviewing requirement, use the provided exception form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAQ references a specific form for requesting exceptions; follow that process rather than emailing program chairs.
